Berth Four fully reopens after quay repairs finish

Nina Halden 15 Oct 2026

Berth Four returned to its full working length of 305 metres today after the final repaired section passed inspection. Work began on 2 September and covered six mooring bollards, eight fenders and the concrete around the bollard foundations. The temporary fencing has been removed.

The completed work cost KRN 8.1 million against an allocation of KRN 8.4 million. The total includes engineering inspections, load tests and disposal of removed materials. Engineers signed off the final three bollards yesterday, and terminal staff completed checks of lighting and quay access before reopening the section.

Both container services temporarily reassigned to Berth Two are now back at Berth Four. Shipping agents have received the updated berth plan. The authority has also closed the temporary pedestrian diversion behind the works. Port users can use the usual marked walkway, while access to the quay edge remains restricted to authorised staff.

Berth Four repairs begin with reduced working area

Nina Halden 2 Sep 2026

Repair work began at Berth Four today after an inspection found worn fittings along the outer quay edge. A 95-metre section has been fenced off while crews replace six mooring bollards and repair the concrete around their foundations. The remaining 210 metres of the berth remain available for smaller vessels.

The authority has allocated KRN 8.4 million to the repairs, including replacement fenders and electrical checks. Two container services normally handled at Berth Four have been assigned to Berth Two. Shipping agents received revised working arrangements this morning, and the published berth list reflects those changes.

A marked pedestrian route runs behind the work area. Port users must keep clear of the fencing and follow instructions from quay staff. The inspection found no damage to the main quay structure. Cargo handling continues elsewhere in the terminal, with no change to freight gate opening hours.

Container volumes rise as inland rail services expand

Mara Venn 21 Aug 2026

The Port of Kestrel Bay handled 84,600 standard container units in July, an increase of 6.2 per cent compared with July last year. Food products, household goods and machine parts accounted for most of the growth. The figures count a forty-foot container as two standard units.

Rail carried 28 per cent of containers leaving the port by land, up from 24 per cent a year earlier. Two additional weekly services between the port and Amberford began operating in June. The inland terminal at Amberford now receives eight port trains each week.

Average lorry turnaround time was 43 minutes during July, measured from entry at the freight gate to departure. This was four minutes shorter than in June. The authority publishes these figures to help hauliers and cargo owners compare port performance. Empty containers and loaded containers are included in the gate measure.

First section of Berth Four returns to service

Nina Halden 18 Sep 2026

A 45-metre section of Berth Four returned to service today following the completion of concrete repairs and load testing on three replacement mooring bollards. The available working length is now 255 metres. The remaining 50 metres of the repair area are still fenced off.

Engineers checked each new bollard under a controlled load before the section was handed back to terminal staff. Four replacement fenders have also been fitted. Spending recorded against the KRN 8.4 million repair allocation stands at KRN 4.1 million, including materials already delivered for the remaining work.

One of the two container services moved to Berth Two has returned to Berth Four. The other remains at Berth Two under the current berth plan. Shipping agents should use the working lengths shown in the port's daily berth list when submitting vessel details. The marked pedestrian route behind the repair area remains in use.

North freight gate reopens after overnight equipment fault

Ellis Corven 26 Aug 2026

The north freight gate at the Port of Kestrel Bay reopened at 09:20 today after a fault in its vehicle recognition equipment. The gate closed at 02:15. Freight traffic used the south entrance while technicians replaced a damaged power unit and checked the control system.

A total of 186 lorry bookings were affected. Drivers with valid bookings were admitted through the south gate without making a second booking, and the authority waived missed-slot charges linked to the closure. The longest recorded queue was 38 vehicles shortly before 07:00. No injuries or damage to cargo were reported.

Both freight entrances are now operating normally. Drivers whose booking records still show a missed visit can ask the gate office to correct the entry, quoting their vehicle registration and booking number. The fault did not affect rail movements, vessel operations or access to the empty-container yard.

Port publishes revised charges for empty container storage

Tomas Bellwick 29 Sep 2026

The Port of Kestrel Bay published a revised empty-container storage tariff today. Under the tariff now in force, the first five calendar days remain free. Storage from day six to day ten costs KRN 18 per standard container unit per day, compared with KRN 15 under the previous tariff.

The rate from day eleven is KRN 31 per unit per day, an increase of KRN 4. Loaded-container storage, vessel dues and rail handling charges are unchanged. Containers already in the empty yard before today remain subject to the previous rates for their current stay.

Empty containers occupied an average of 81 per cent of designated yard spaces during August. The revised charges follow a tariff review circulated to account holders in July. Customers can view the applicable rate and arrival date for each container in their account record, or request a written breakdown from the port billing team.

Rail signalling fault delays inland container departures today

Ellis Corven 13 Oct 2026

A signalling fault at Reedbank Junction interrupted freight rail access to the Port of Kestrel Bay today. The junction operator stopped movements at 06:25 after a track detection circuit failed. Three outbound trains carrying a combined 144 containers were held in the port rail yard.

One train was bound for Amberford and two for the Saltmarsh inland terminal. The line reopened at 13:40 following replacement of the faulty component and a test movement. The first delayed train left the port at 14:05. No containers were transferred to road transport during the closure.

Rail customers received revised departure details through their booking contacts. Containers held on the affected trains have been exempted from additional port storage charges caused by the interruption. Vessel loading and unloading continued throughout the incident, and freight gates remained open. The fault occurred outside the port boundary and did not affect the terminal's internal rail equipment.

September figures show shorter queues at freight gates

Mara Venn 5 Oct 2026

Average lorry turnaround time at the Port of Kestrel Bay fell to 39 minutes in September, compared with 43 minutes in July. The monthly figure covers 31,480 completed visits and includes time spent waiting inside the terminal. Visits cancelled before arrival are excluded.

The port handled 82,900 standard container units during September. This was 2.4 per cent above the same month last year, despite the wind stoppage on 3 September and the reduced working length at Berth Four. Rail accounted for 29 per cent of containers leaving the port by land.

Gate staff recorded fewer arrivals without bookings after hauliers began receiving an additional booking reminder in August. Unbooked arrivals fell from 412 in August to 267 in September. The authority asks drivers to check the container release status before travelling, as a gate booking alone does not confirm that cargo is ready for collection.

Strong winds interrupt crane operations across container terminal

Ellis Corven 3 Sep 2026

Container crane operations at the Port of Kestrel Bay were suspended between 05:40 and 11:10 today after wind speeds exceeded the terminal's operating limit. Instruments on the quay recorded gusts of 78 kilometres per hour. Cranes were secured, and staff were withdrawn from exposed working areas.

Three vessels experienced delays, including one using the reduced working area at Berth Four. By 14:00, all operational cranes had returned to service following safety checks. Shipping agents have received revised departure estimates based on the remaining cargo moves for each vessel.

Freight gates remained open, but some drivers waited longer while container lifts were paused. The authority cancelled waiting charges for vehicles held inside the terminal during the suspension. No injuries, dropped containers or damage to lifting equipment were reported. Repair crews at Berth Four also stopped exposed work during the strongest winds.
